learning_outcomes.text: Application of the basic theoretical principles underlying fluidomechanical machines and systems
Initiative to undertake new developments and applications in educational innovation projects
Ability to classify different fluid machines and their scope of use
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluidomechanical systems and machines.
Design of fluidomechanical systems, optimization and improvements

syllabus_topics: Definitions and classification of fluid and hydraulic machines
Rayleigh's dissipation function and power dissipation of viscous forces
Variation of fluid temperature between the inlet and outlet of the hydraulic machine
Specific energies for hydraulic motor machines
Specific energies for hydraulic generating machines
Powers and efficiencies in hydraulic machines
Conservation of angular momentum. First Euler equation
Interpretation of the second Euler equation.
Influence of the distributor on hydraulic efficiency
HYDROELECTRIC POWER PLANTS AND TURBINE REGULATION
Definition and classification of hydroelectric power plants
Regulation of a hydroelectric power plant
Wind power absorbed by the rotor. Power coefficient. Betz limit
Influential aspects in wind energy capture. Capacity factor
Definitions and classification. Typology of hydraulic pumps
Energy transfer in rotodynamic pumps. Pump heads
Cavitation in pumps. Suction head limitation
Modification of curves. Effects of density, viscosity, passage of time, etc.
Static and dynamic loads. Applied Euler equation. Types of fans
Piston pumps. Irregularity. Coupling, multi-cylinder pumps
Powers and efficiencies. Calculation of basic dimensions
Functions of a hydraulic equipment. Applications
Main components of a hydraulic system. Symbology and diagrams
Applications. Development of an oleohydraulic control system
Test of impulse turbines. Characteristic curves
Test of reaction turbines. Characteristic curves
Test of cavitation in centrifugal pumps
Series and parallel association of pumps
Wind tunnel: measurement of lift and drag on an airfoil
assessment_rules: By default, the progressive evaluation system will be followed. The final grade is calculated as 40% Written Test 1 + 50% Written Test 2 + 10% Lab Exam. All evaluation activities require a minimum grade of 3.0/10 to be considered in the weighted average, and the overall grade must be 5 or higher to pass. In the case of not passing, lab attendance and the lab exam grade are conserved if the student attended and completed the exam. Alternatively, a global exam option is available, where the final grade is 90% Global Written Exam + 10% Lab Exam, with the Lab Exam also requiring a minimum of 3.0/10. The extraordinary exam (resit) follows the global exam criteria.
